newsitem.title: FRANCE: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - July 9.
newsitem.headline: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - July 9.

text.p: REUTERS FRENCH ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and People News.
ADVERTISING, MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

PARIS - Euro RSCG Gregoire-Blachere-Houard-Roussel and Ammirati Puris Lintas are the two finalists in the competition for the advertising account of Air France, estimated at 200 million francs ($33.7 million). (Le Figaro)

AMSTERDAM - Canal Plus, the French pay television group, says its Dutch subsidiary is to pay 145 million guilders ($73.2 million) over the next five years for the rights to show live Dutch first division football matches. (Reuter)

PARIS - France 2, the biggest French public television channel, says it had a net loss of 199.3 million francs in 1996 compared with a net profit of 60.7 million francs in 1995. The loss was much bigger than a forecast published in Le Monde newspaper last month of a 70- million-franc loss. (Reuter)

PARIS - ART, the French telecommunications regulator, will give a first verdict on Friday on a dispute over how much France Telecom should be able to charge cable TV companies to use its cable networks for Internet access. (La Tribune, Le Figaro)

PARIS - A French strike on Tuesday at press distribution depots took all national daily papers off the streets, even though the distribution workers' grievance is over changes in periodical distribution. (Le Figaro, Liberation)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

PARIS - The French index of consumer sentiment rises to minus 23 in June from minus 33 in May, a marked improvement after having hovered around minus 30 for several months, according to national statistics institute INSEE. (Reuter)
PARIS - Some 11 percent of French households live below the poverty line, a figure just under the European Union average of 11.8 percent, a study by INSEE shows.(Reuter)

MONTREAL - Sommer Allibert, a French company that makes fitted furniture, says it plans to sue Armstrong World Industries Inc for allegedly violating confidentiality agreements between the two rival companies. Armstrong says it is seeking an injunction to block the merger of Sommer Allibert and Tarkett AG of Germany. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:

PARIS - Henri Morny, director of international affairs and research and development for Socpresse, the parent company of French press group Hersant, died on Monday of a heart attack. He was 68. (Le Figaro)

PARIS - Gerard Unger has been appointed chairman of Metrobus and vice-chairman of Metrovision following the purchase by Publicis of Havas's shares in the two advertising groups. Unger was previously vice-chairman of Publicis Communications in charge of its French units. (Le Figaro)
